guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, sw_key_data_reg[1] is asynchronously cleared to all zeros.

When engine_stable is high, on the next posedge clk_i, for every j in [0, MaxKeyLen/32-1] where reg2hw.key_share1[j].qe is high, the corresponding 32-bit segment sw_key_data_reg[1][32*j+:32] takes the value of reg2hw.key_share1[j].q from the previous cycle.
When rst_ni is high and engine_stable is low, sw_key_data_reg[1] holds its previous value (no update).

assumptions.claim: While engine_stable is asserted, the values of reg2hw.key_share1[*].q and .qe must remain stable so that the captured key word is deterministic and consistent.
assumptions.risk: A glitch or change on key_share1 during capture may cause a corrupted or mismatched key word to be stored in sw_key_data_reg[1].

assumptions.claim: MaxKeyLen is a positive integer multiple of 32, and sw_key_data_reg[1] is dimensioned to hold at least MaxKeyLen bits so that the for loop indexing does not overflow.
assumptions.risk: Misparameterization could cause out-of-bounds writes into sw_key_data_reg[1], leading to functional failure or corruption of adjacent logic.

uncertain_points.claim: Only sw_key_data_reg[1] (key share 1) is cleared on reset. It is unclear whether other key shares (e.g., sw_key_data_reg[0]) must also be zeroized to meet security requirements for secret key wipe.
uncertain_points.risk: If the key is split into multiple shares, residual key material in uncleared shares may leak the key value after reset.

formal_sketch.consequent: Only sw_key_data_reg[1] (key share 1) is cleared on reset. It is unclear whether other key shares (e.g., sw_key_data_reg[0]) must also be zeroized to meet security requirements for secret key wipe

uncertain_points.claim: If engine_stable is asserted for more than one cycle and reg2hw.key_share1[*].qe toggles between cycles, partial key word updates can occur, potentially leaving sw_key_data_reg[1] with a mix of old and new key words.

uncertain_points.risk: Inconsistent key material in sw_key_data_reg[1] may lead to cryptographic errors or exposure if the incomplete key is used prematurely.

security_implications: sw_key_data_reg[1] (key share 1) is cleared on reset, but other key shares are not cleared in this chunk. If key is split into multiple shares, residual secret material in uncleared shares may survive reset and leak the key. Additionally, the engine_stable handshake and key_share1 capture have no explicit guarding against partial or glitched updates, which could corrupt the key or expose a timing side channel.
